| **Assessed** | 2026-11-27 |

AI adds half a point a year to US productivity growth for 30 years and the extra income is shared in proportion to existing incomes. GDP is 16% higher by 2056 and federal debt ends 39 points of GDP below the CBO baseline.

## Social contract scores (draft)

| Promise | Score | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hard work pays | 4 | No fall in the number of workers and labour income rises in proportion across the whole distribution, a modest gain of about 16% after 30 years. |
| Affordable essentials |  | Not addressed: the extract has only a conditional note that faster healthcare cost growth would raise Medicare Part B premiums, and no price path for housing, food, energy or care. |
| Reliable safety net | 3 | No job losses test the net, and under current law benefits keep their real value while retirees and lower-income households fall behind relative to rising incomes, which the authors flag as a possible weakening. |
| Responsive government | 3 | Faster growth offsets about half the projected debt rise, leaving elected policymakers a real choice over the size of government, but debt still rises and public support for tax rises or benefit cuts is limited. |
| Time for what matters |  | Not addressed: the authors explicitly set aside the case where workers take gains as more leisure. |
